doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Opening and festival set choices
summary: Monk Rowe opens the filming and asks about the gentle, slow tunes each chose for their solo spots at the festival.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: Good afternoon. We are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. My name is Monk Rowe, and it’s a great pleasure today to have two guests who are fixtures in the jazz scene, especially on the west coast here. Can I call you guys “fixtures?”
Saxophonist and arranger Tommy Newsom and keyboardist Ross Tompkins. Welcome, gentlemen.

We’ve been fortunate to listen to the music you’ve been creating before we talk today so I kind of have a starting place. The group you’re working with right now, the fellows that you’ve been with for quite a while thanks to the Tonight Show, and you can really tell in the music. I was interested last night in that when you each did your solo spot that you picked something very, kind of gentle and slow tempo.
I know I did. Well there’s a level of activity around a jazz festival that tends to be on the frenetic side sometimes.
Yeah. Especially with all the Dixieland going on too.
